candidates.title: PRT stored player retains only 32 input boundaries per epoch, so an input flood makes every match's bundle opening, uarch-claim build and leaf proof replay ~3/64 of the epoch's inputs
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua stored player: machine cache, agreed pair), run by crisium.lua
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); it is the implementation of an operator that computes claims, so it stands in for the honest operator (THREAT_MODEL section 3).
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: STORED_MACHINE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 32 (line 901) and the comment at 899-900 ('keeps more input boundaries, so reaching a disputed input replays only a few inputs'); machine_cache_methods:consider (1217-1245, gap doubling when full); new_stored_machine_cache (1334-1345); find_nearest_entry (1247-1258); player_meta.__index:new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset (2055-2060) and stored_player_methods:new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset (3040-3052); run_to_epoch_input_offset (2150-2172, one delivery + run + stored_machine_pair_methods:commit per replayed input, 1121-1134); callers on the per-match path: collect_mcycle_bundle (2296, bundle opening during the mcycle bisection), build_uarch_cycle_computation_hash (2315), collect_uarch_cycle_bundle (2334), event_handler.prove_state_transition (1956). Single agreed pair / single recorded bisection: stored_event_handler.reveal_bisection/seal_divergence (3029-3037) overwrite self.bisection; advance_agreed_pair (2984-3017) drops the pair whenever the latest bisection lies elsewhere.
candidates.description: The stored player keeps at most 32 machines at input boundaries for the whole epoch. When the cache is full and no entry is closer than input_gap to its predecessor, the gap doubles, so after n inputs the entries are spaced n/32..n/16 apart. Every operation a match forces on the honest claim that needs a machine (opening an mcycle bundle when the bisection reaches it, building the uarch claim, collecting a uarch bundle, logging the leaf transition) starts from find_nearest_entry and replays every input between that entry and the disputed input, each replay doing a delivery, a run to the fixed point and a full stored-pair commit (destroy, sync, clone to .revert, sync, load). The only mitigation is one agreed pair advanced one input per idle step, and only for the most recent bisection: with several matches (Sybils at different positions) it is dropped and rebuilt. So the cost of reaching a disputed position grows linearly with the number of inputs in the epoch (worst case about 3n/64 inputs: 47 inputs at n=1024, 3,071 at 2^16, 49,151 at 2^20, 786,431 at 2^24) instead of being bounded by one input's usage. THREAT_MODEL R12 states the bound the honest operator must meet: 'Each is measured from a machine at its starting position. Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds. A7 must cover that cost a bounded number of times for every match', and 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match'. Retaining every boundary is what R12 allows (storage may grow with the inputs of open epochs; stored clones are reflinks), but the player trades it for a per-match replay that grows with the input count, contrary also to its own comment 'reaching a disputed input replays only a few inputs'.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender (THREAT_MODEL section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'). The adversary floods the epoch with many cheap inputs (empty payloads are enough; a correctly designed application accepts them), then posts Sybil claims that steer matches to positions far from the retained boundaries (any input just before the next cache entry). Each match makes the honest player replay up to ~3n/64 inputs before it can answer a bisection step at bundle level, build its uarch claim within the inner COMMITMENT_BUDGET (120 minutes in the released Dave constants), or log the leaf transition.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: only the number of inputs (bounded by DaveConsensus to 2^24 per epoch) and the dispute positions, both adversary-controlled, matter. No unusual guest behavior is needed.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No. The trigger is the input count and the dispute positions, which section 7 grants the adversary. The exclusion 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields' covers outputs and yields, not inputs. The player is in scope (only the sling node and the Rollups node are excluded). 2. Role: the PRT player is Support (AUDIT.md table). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' So rate it as an honest operator, then cap at Medium. 3. High/Medium cases, honest-operator role: the High case 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor' does not fit: the factor (about 3n/64 inputs instead of one) grows with the adversary's input count, so it is not constant ('When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High and a super-linear or unbounded one Critical'). 4. Critical, honest-operator role: violates R12 on the honest operator's path at a reachable state: 'Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds. A7 must cover that cost a bounded number of times for every match', and 'has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match'. A cost per match that grows with the input count can exceed the clocks (A7: 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock' presumes the honest operator's per-match cost is the sized one). As support, capped: Medium. 5. n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; Critical if a production honest operator used this cache policy)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness: an adversary who floods an epoch and steers Sybil matches to positions far from retained boundaries makes the honest player spend hours replaying inputs per match (about 0.29 s per input measured for the echo template, so ~4 h at n=2^20), so it misses bisection deadlines or the 120-minute inner commitment budget and the honest claim is eliminated by timeout, after which a dishonest claim can win (section 1: 'cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win').
candidates.evidence: Code reading of prt.lua (paths above). Replicated machine_cache_methods:consider with capacity 32 in a scratch script (scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFINPUTCOUNT/cache-gap.lua): worst inputs replayed to reach a slot = 0 (n=32), 47 (n=1024), 3071 (n=2^16), 49151 (n=2^20), 786431 (n=2^24); final gap 2^19 at n=2^24. Measured the replay unit that run_to_epoch_input_offset executes per input (delivery of an empty-payload EvmAdvance, run to the manual yield, stored-pair commit) on the XFS reflink mount (replay-cost.lua): valid-template (Linux echo app) 0.227 s run + 0.064 s commit per input; baremetal-template 0.013 s + 0.035 s.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: create a stored player with prt.new_stored_player on a copy of the baremetal-template (or valid-template) in the XFS mount, deliver N=512 empty-payload inputs through stored_event_handler.input_added + idle, seal with epoch_sealed(N). Wrap player.run_to_input_mcycle_offset (a method looked up through the player's metatable, so it can be shadowed on the instance) to count calls, then call player:new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset(k) for the k just before the second-to-last cache entry (or call event_handler.prove_state_transition(player, k, 0, 0)). Assert the number of inputs replayed is at most a constant independent of N (for example <= 1, as R12's 'nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds' requires). It currently replays about 3N/64 (24 for N=512) and fails; repeating with N=1024 shows the count doubling.

candidates.title: PRT player's epoch-0 listener fetches InputAdded only from the consensus deployment block, but DaveConsensus seals into epoch 0 every input the application already had, so the player crash-loops on 'sealed input count mismatch'
candidates.component: PRT player process: doc/recipes/crisium.lua (epoch listener setup) with doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua (epoch listener); compared with Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 DaveConsensus constructor
candidates.role: Support (crisium.lua and prt-epoch.lua belong to the PRT player and bridge). DaveConsensus (referee model) behaves as written; the defect is in the player's assignment of inputs to epoch 0.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua:125 (first_block = consensus.getDeploymentBlockNumber()), :247 (input_begin = 0 for epoch 0), :265-267 (first_input_block = previous_seal and previous_seal.log.blockNumber or first_block); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua:36-37 (history:get_logs(address, self.first_input_block, ...)), :95-98 (assert sealed bounds), :167. bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol constructor (inputIndexUpperBound = _nextInputIndexUpperBound(0), i.e. min(InputBox.getNumberOfInputs(app), 2^24)), _nextInputIndexUpperBound.
candidates.description: DaveConsensus seals epoch 0 in its constructor with inputs [0, min(getNumberOfInputs(app), 2^24)), so every input the application received before the consensus existed belongs to epoch 0. crisium starts the epoch-0 listener at the consensus deployment block, so InputAdded logs from earlier blocks are never fetched. When the listener applies EpochSealed(0) it asserts inputIndexUpperBound == input_begin + #inputs (0) and raises 'sealed input count mismatch'; prt-supervise relaunches the process, which fails the same way, so every epoch stops. It is the epoch-0 variant (the 'or first_block' branch) of round 1's backlog candidate R1-A3-1, which concerns the previous-seal block of later epochs. Inputs can exist before the consensus whenever the application was not created atomically with it: rollups-contracts' ApplicationFactory accepts any outputsMerkleRootValidator address (for example the precomputed CREATE2 address of a DaveConsensus deployed later), migrateToOutputsMerkleRootValidator is allowed in the application's deployment block, and InputBox.addInput accepts inputs for any deployed, non-foreclosed application. DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp creates both in one transaction and cannot reach it.
candidates.trigger: The deployer creates the application (ApplicationFactory) with its validator set to the future DaveConsensus address and deploys DaveConsensus in a later block. Any input sender adds inputs to the application in between. Then the honest PRT player is started for the application.
candidates.reachability: Requires a deployment that is not made by DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp, but uses only released, permissionless contracts and their documented entry points (ApplicationFactory.newApplication with an arbitrary validator, a DaveConsensus constructed directly). The player itself discovers everything 'from the application's address alone' (prt-lua-bridge.md) and does not refuse such an application. Whether triage treats this deployment as one the player must support decides the rating.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Not by the trigger list: inputs are sent by untrusted parties, and DaveConsensus (the deployed referee) assigns them consistently with A3 (at most 2^24 per epoch). If triage reads the non-factory deployment as outside what the recipe supports, it is Low (a defect that violates no rule for supported deployments). 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md: PRT player and bridge). Section 3: 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3. High/Medium cases for the honest operator: none fits. 4. Critical for the honest operator: R4 'It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)' and section 8 Critical 'A crash, hang ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process' (the on-chain input record). Capped as support: Medium. 5. Low if the deployment is deemed unsupported.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support), or Low if the deployment shape is deemed unsupported
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness: the honest player cannot assign the on-chain input record to epoch 0, crashes before joining epoch 0's tournament and keeps crashing after each relaunch, so it never defends epoch 0 or any later epoch and a dishonest claim wins by default.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: DaveConsensus constructor and _nextInputIndexUpperBound; rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 InputBox.addInput (only notForeclosed(app), which requires code and isForeclosed()==0), Application.migrateToOutputsMerkleRootValidator (onlyOwner, notForeclosed, onDeploymentBlock); crisium.lua and prt-epoch.lua as cited. No chain experiment run.
candidates.test_idea: Chain test (bugs/harness/chain, released or patched Dave): deploy an Application with ApplicationFactory.newApplication whose validator is the CREATE2 address of a DaveConsensus to be deployed by a small deployer contract, add 2 inputs through InputBox, mine a few blocks, deploy the DaveConsensus at that address (EpochSealed(0, 0, 2, ...)), store the epoch-0 checkpoint and run crisium.lua --kind=honest for a bounded time. Assert that it processes InputAdded 0 and 1 for epoch 0, passes the seal check and commits its epoch-0 claim. It currently exits with 'sealed input count mismatch'. Without a chain: build prt-epoch.new with first_input_block as crisium computes it, and a fake chain/log history holding the two InputAdded logs in a block before first_block and EpochSealed(0, 0, 2) at first_block. Assert that poll() delivers both inputs and does not raise.

not_covered: No chain experiment: the input-flood scenario was not run against Dave on anvil. Candidate 1's evidence is a replica of the cache policy plus measured per-input replay costs. Candidate 2 is from code reading only.

Did not measure how far the agreed-pair idle advancement offsets candidate 1 in a real bisection, given block times and the bridge's deadlines. Did not quantify the number of Sybil matches the released Dave clocks let an adversary force per epoch.

Dave Tournament leaf/inner-tournament lifetime after an epoch settles (provideMerkleRootOfInput reads the current sealed epoch's bounds; round 1 believed this harmless). Not re-examined beyond confirming that ROOT_WINNER requires matchCount == 0 in the root.
machine-guest-tools handling of maximum-size (64 KiB) and empty-payload inputs in libcmt/rollup/rollup-http-server: source fetched, io.c read, rest not audited (round 1 GUEST hunter covered libcmt).
The referee model's (prt.lua/game-transport.lua) notify_all of input_added/epoch_sealed waits FOREVER for every subscriber. Noted as a variant of R1-A8-3's stall class (support), not reported.

The listener and bridge keep every input's bytes of an open epoch in Lua memory (self.inputs), so RAM grows with total input bytes (up to 2^24 x 64 KiB). R12 permits growth with the inputs of open epochs, so it was not reported, and it was not measured.
Gas and calldata of the maximum-size delivery proof under real per-transaction limits (round 1 A3 measured the size only).
The cartesi-machine CLI epoch driver with more than 2^24 input files: needs a trusted caller's misuse, so not pursued.

Emulator delivery no-op rules (send_cmio_response C++, regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol, machine API checks, Lua bindings) were read and found consistent with R5, including oversized, zero-length and non-accepted-yield cases. No EVM run of the no-op branches.
Rust/sling node and Cartesi Rollups Node input assignment (out of scope).
